qa.q: Which branch do I develop on, and where does the built release live?
qa.answer: Develop on `v2`. CI builds the `release` branch (orphan, built output only, no package.json). `main` stays frozen at the last v1 version so v1's /ctx-upgrade sees no change.

qa.q: What is the DB path and schema I create in M0?
qa.answer: One SQLite file: ~/.context-mode/projects/<git-common-dir-hash>/context.db. Tables: events, sources, chunks (FTS5), meta. Engine node:sqlite, {timeout:5000}, every write starts BEGIN IMMEDIATE, no retry loop.
qa.docGap: storage.json (blocker): PRD-v2.md §4 (lines 75-84) still describes the old per-session-DB model and a '--fix deletes only that session DB' rule, which deletes everything in the new shared-DB model. ADR-0002 also has no corruption policy for the single file. Fix PRD §4 and add a corruption rule to ADR-0002 before coding storage.

qa.q: What MCP protocol version do I target, and how do I read the client's identity (agent name)?
qa.answer: Target spec 2026-07-28, but keep answering 2025-xx initialize clients. Read agent identity from the SDK's normal accessor.
qa.docGap: mcp.json (blocker): ADR-0007 decision 4 as written says identity comes only from each request's _meta. Claude Code (2025-11-25) and Codex (2025-06-18) send clientInfo once, in initialize, and never again, so this text would re-break issue #542. Fix ADR-0007 decision 4 to say: clientInfo from initialize params for 2025-xx sessions, from _meta for 2026-07-28 requests, one shared accessor. Needed before writing the agent-detection module.

qa.q: What are the exact tool names I register, and what are the hard size limits?
qa.answer: 9 tools: ctx_execute, ctx_batch, ctx_index, ctx_search, ctx_resume, ctx_stats, ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade, ctx_purge. Limits: instructions <= 2048 chars, each tool description <= 1024 chars, all descriptions + schemas <= 8000 chars.

qa.q: How does the Bash-enforcement hook decide allow/deny/rewrite? Do I write regex?
qa.answer: No regex, by owner rule. Write a real shell parser (lexer + recursive descent, about 12 KB, 1.26 ms) that reads each simple command's argv0 and parsed flags. Deny only when a command's body reaches stdout. Constructs the parser can't handle ([[, ((, case, functions, process substitution) are allowed and logged as a ParseError code.
qa.evidence: ADR-0008 'What changes' table row 1, and 'Parse errors' section
qa.docGap: hooks-perf.json (major): ADR-0008 says 'Claude Code starts no process' for its hook, but this is only true for PreToolUse/PostToolUse (mcp_tool). Claude Code's SessionStart hook at launch/--continue/--resume must be a type:"command" hook and pays bare-Node startup time, which has no budget row yet. Fix ADR-0008 (or the adapter table) with a per-event transport row before building the SessionStart hook.

qa.q: When output is too big, do I cut it, or pick parts of it?
qa.answer: Never cut or truncate, by owner rule. Index the full output in context.db, then select whole chunks that best match the call's intent by BM25 score under a byte budget (budgeted greedy). Always end with one 'more:' line the caller can run itself.

qa.q: Inside a subagent that only has Bash/Read (no ctx tools), how do I keep a big command's output out of its context?
qa.answer: Case B (has Bash): PreToolUse rewrites the command to run through the wrapper unchanged, indexes the full output, returns matched chunks + a 'more:' line the subagent's own Bash can run. Case C (no Bash either): PostToolUse replaces the tool's output the same way. An unknown built-in subagent type is always treated as case B or C, never a plain allow, until live check LV8 confirms its tool set.
qa.docGap: ADR-0016 itself: the mechanism is 'Proposed' status until live checks LV8-LV10 pass. Code to the conservative no-ctx-tools default until those checks land; do not assume LV8's tool-set table yet.

qa.q: What test runner and Node matrix do I target, and does v2 use npm at all?
qa.answer: Test runner is node:test against built .mjs files, matrix 3 OS x min/current Node, <=10 min per OS. No npm install at runtime and no npm publish for v2 distribution.
qa.docGap: qa.json (blocker): Q9 fixes the runner as node:test, but the owner decision keeps v1's vitest+TypeScript unit tests alive until the kept parts pass, so vitest must also stay in devDependencies and CI; TECH-SPEC never says this. Also ADR-0002 flags the minimum Node version for stable node:sqlite as never checked (open spike S-NODE). Fix TECH-SPEC §9/Q9 to cover both runners, and close spike S-NODE, before setting up CI.

qa.q: Do I delete v1's tests/ folder in M0?
qa.answer: No. Owner decision: v1 unit tests stay; keep building v2 until the tests covering kept parts pass on v2, plus the new E2E suite.
qa.evidence: user rule (this conversation's standing instruction) and tickets/v2-test-ledger.md intent

qa.q: On Windows, how do I kill a timed-out child process tree with no native addon?
qa.answer: Use taskkill /F /T /PID, the same mechanism v1 already uses and that is proven to work. Do not build a Job Object path; Node has no Job Object API and a native addon would break the no-native-binding decision.
qa.evidence: windows.json finding fix note; v1 src/executor.ts:196-206
qa.docGap: windows.json (major/blocker): TECH-SPEC §8 and PRD-v2.md:138 still say 'Windows Job Object' with no build path named. Fix TECH-SPEC §8 and PRD-v2.md:138 to state taskkill /F /T explicitly, and add a GP4 Windows golden case (grandchild process killed on timeout), before writing the executor's kill code.

qa.q: Does the user's existing permissions.deny (e.g. a denied Bash rm -rf pattern) also block the same command when it is sent through ctx_execute?
qa.answer: It must. v1 checked the same deny policy at the server layer for ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file and ctx_batch_execute, not only at the hook layer.
qa.evidence: ADR-0001 'deny comes only from the user's policy file'

As written, a Bash deny rule in .claude/settings.json would not stop the same command sent to ctx_execute, reopening the bypass v1 closed. Fix ADR-0008 and PRD G6 to name the ctx tools as deny-checked before coding the sandbox executor.

qa.q: What exactly must the bug issue template collect from the agent reading it, and what is the governing rule?
qa.answer: The template is written for an AI agent, not a human; the agent reading it must follow our rules and send us maximum debug data. ADR-0014 bug.yml: tell the agent to run /ctx-doctor first (or call the ctx_doctor tool); a dropdown 'did doctor run?' with fixed No-reasons; a required doctor-report textarea (render: text); a required `node --version` field; what happened / expected / steps, where steps must name the exact tool that was denied and the alternative it was given; 2 required checkboxes. No pull-request template; CONTRIBUTING.md says issues only, with the doctor report attached.
qa.docGap: ADR-0014 is still status 'Proposed,' not yet Accepted. Confirm it is accepted before wiring the GitHub issue forms or CI around it.

qa.q: What does the ctx_doctor debug report contain, and how is it kept safe to paste into a public issue (no secrets)?
qa.answer: A fixed list of key:value lines, starting 'ctx-report: 1' and ending 'digest: <sha256>', at most 4096 bytes by construction (worst case 2652 B / 38 lines). Redaction is by structure, not regex: every value must pass a typed scanner (int, semver, hex40, date, enum, bool, or a JSON pointer into our own schema); anything that fails becomes '<invalid>' and is dropped whole, never cut. Paths, env values, file bodies and command lines can never reach the output. The server never statically imports node:sqlite, so ctx_doctor still answers even in a degraded start.

qa.q: How do I detect leftover v1 files per agent for ctx_doctor/ctx_upgrade, and is this a fallback chain (which is banned)?
qa.answer: Not a fallback chain: one pure detectV1(agent) function per agent, returning {file, path, reason}, that never edits anything. ctx_doctor reports what it finds; ctx_upgrade removes it. The exact file/path list per agent is a fixed table, not a search order.
qa.docGap: v1-migration-sim.json + release-premortem.json (blocker): the marketplace-ref switch (ADR-0011 step b) edits only .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Codex reads .agents/plugins/marketplace.json first, whose source stays './' on main, so Codex users who added the marketplace with no ref either stay on frozen v1 forever or later get the raw v2 source tree instead of the release build. Fix ADR-0011 step b to also update the Codex marketplace file on main, before scripting the release runbook.

qa.q: What is the compaction/session-state format, and do I need to build any memory injection or role classifier?
qa.answer: One session-keyed state block, at most 2 KB after compaction, stored at a per-agent path. Resume is a single hint line. No injected memory, and no role/intent classifier — do not build either.
qa.evidence: PRD-v2.md §16 'Compaction'; ADR-0009 (referenced size figure in hooks-perf.json: 'the whole SessionStart process is 48.6 ms p95')
qa.docGap: I read ADR-0009 only through citations in other review files, not its full body. Re-read ADR-0009 directly before coding the compaction writer, in case it has detail beyond the PRD line.
